Regular time-harmonic spherical wave (u(r,t)=Asin(ωt)sin(ωr/c)/(ωr/c))

Words: 74
Wave equation OurBigBook.com
For a spherically symmetric function, v=ru reduces the radial wave equation to vtt​=c2vrr​. A time-harmonic separated solution has radial numerator Csin(kr)+Dcos(kr), with k=ω/c. Finiteness at the origin excludes D, and the prescribed finite origin value fixes C. This is a standing combination of incoming and outgoing waves. A purely outgoing point-source wave instead has a 1/r singularity and must be specified by its source strength, not by a finite value at the origin.

Retarded acoustic Green function (GR​(r,t)=δ(t−r/c0​)/(4πc02​r))

Words: 25
Wave equation OurBigBook.com
This is the causal three-dimensional fundamental solution of ∂t2​−c02​∇2. It concentrates on the outgoing sound cone and gives the retarded convolution of acoustic sources.

All-time boundedness of a wave equation with a reaction term (α<λ1​)

Words: 73
Wave equation OurBigBook.com
For utt​=Δu+αu with a homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition, let λ1​>0 be the first Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalue. On a bounded one-dimensional interval, finite-energy displacement remains bounded for all time and all initial data exactly when α<λ1​. The conserved energy 21​(∥ut​∥22​+∥∇u∥22​−α∥u∥22​) controls the gradient and, by the Poincaré inequality and one-dimensional integration, the maximum norm. At equality a mode can grow linearly; above it a mode can grow exponentially. Bounded oscillations need not have a long-time limit.

Vector field method for wave equations

Words: 254 Articles: 7
Wave equation OurBigBook.com
The vector field method commutes a wave equation with spacetime symmetry generators, estimates the resulting commuted wave energies, and converts weighted L2 norms to pointwise decay using a Klainerman-Sobolev inequality. The commutation vector fields for the wave equation include translations, rotations, Lorentz boost vector fields and the scaling vector field. It is useful for almost global existence for wave equations and for small-data global existence under the classical null condition for wave equations.

Commuted wave energy (Am​(t)=∑∣I∣≤m​∥∂ZIu(t)∥2​)

Words: 37
Vector field method for wave equations OurBigBook.com
A commuted wave energy controls derivatives of a solution after applying the commutation vector fields for the wave equation. A convenient equivalent norm is Am​(t)=∑∣I∣≤m​∥∂ZIu(t)∥2​. The wave energy estimate controls its growth through commuted sources, while the Klainerman-Sobolev inequality gives pointwise decay for low-order derivatives.

Klainerman-Sobolev inequality (∣u∣≲(1+t+r)(1+∣t−r∣)1/2∑∣I∣≤2​∥ZIu∥2​​)

Words: 38
Vector field method for wave equations OurBigBook.com
In three spatial dimensions, with Z the eleven translations, spatial rotations, boosts and scaling commutation vector fields for the wave equation, a sufficiently decaying smooth function satisfies ∣u(t,x)∣≤C(1+t+∣x∣)−1(1+∣t−∣x∣∣)−1/2∑∣I∣≤2​∥ZIu(t)∥2​. This weighted Sobolev inequality converts control of commuted wave energy into decay. It holds independently of any wave equation satisfied by u.

Commutation vector field for the wave equation

Words: 137 Articles: 4
Vector field method for wave equations OurBigBook.com
A first-order vector field Z is a commutation field for the flat wave equation when [□,Z] is zero or a controlled multiple of □. Translations, spatial rotations and Lorentz boost vector fields commute with □; the scaling vector field satisfies [□,S]=2□. Repeated commutation preserves the differential order of a semilinear wave equation.

Scaling vector field (S=t∂t​+x⋅∇)

Words: 30
Commutation vector field for the wave equation OurBigBook.com
The vector field S=t∂t​+x⋅∇ generates simultaneous spacetime dilation. For the flat d'Alembert operator, [□,S]=2□. Consequently it commutes with the homogeneous wave equation at the level of its solution set, although its operator commutator is nonzero.

Lorentz boost vector field (Li​=t∂i​+xi​∂t​)

Words: 23
Commutation vector field for the wave equation OurBigBook.com
For Minkowski spacetime with unit light speed, Li​=t∂i​+xi​∂t​ generates a Lorentz boost. It commutes with the d'Alembert operator and controls derivatives transverse to time slices in the vector field method for wave equations.

Spatial rotation vector field (Ωij​=xi​∂j​−xj​∂i​)

Words: 19
Commutation vector field for the wave equation OurBigBook.com
The vector field Ωij​=xi​∂j​−xj​∂i​ is an infinitesimal spatial rotation. It commutes with the flat d'Alembert operator and supplies angular derivatives in the Klainerman-Sobolev inequality.

Spacetime translation vector field (∂μ​)

Words: 23
Commutation vector field for the wave equation OurBigBook.com
The vector fields ∂t​ and ∂i​ generate time and space translations and commute with the flat d'Alembert operator. They form the unweighted part of the commutation vector fields for the wave equation.

Wave energy (Elin​=21​∫(∣ut​∣2+∣∇u∣2)dx)

Words: 29
Wave equation OurBigBook.com
For a real scalar wave equation, the kinetic and gradient energy is Elin​(t)=21​∫(∣ut​∣2+∣∇u∣2)dx. A potential term is added for a semilinear wave equation utt​−Δu+V′(u)=0, giving the conserved wave energy E=Elin​+∫V(u)dx.

Reflected-step solution of the wave equation (y(x,t))

Words: 78
Wave equation OurBigBook.com
For ytt​=c2yxx​ on 0<x<L, initially at rest with zero displacement, apply y(0,t)=a for t>0 and keep y(L,t)=0. A geometric series in the Laplace transform gives
y(x,t)=a∑m≥0​[H(t−c2mL+x​)−H(t−c(2m+2)L−x​)].
(1)
Here H is the Heaviside step function, L,c>0, and only finitely many terms contribute at any finite time. The second step in each pair is a sign-reversed reflection from the fixed endpoint. The formula solves the wave equation classically away from the fronts and distributionally across them; the midpoint is a square wave of period 2L/c.

Wave speed (c)

Wave equation OurBigBook.com
The wave speed c is the propagation speed in a wave equation such as utt​=c2∇2u.

Slowness (s=1/v)

Words: 36
Wave speed OurBigBook.com
Slowness is the reciprocal of phase velocity, measured in time per distance. A plane wave with wavevector k and angular frequency ω has vector slowness p=k/ω. Its direction is the wavefront normal, which need not be the group velocity direction in an anisotropic medium.

Wave equation OurBigBook.com
In three spatial dimensions, the solution with initial position u0​ and velocity u1​ is
u(t,x)=∂t​(tMt​u0​(x))+tMt​u1​(x),
(2)
where Mt​ is the spherical mean.

Method of descent for the wave equation

Words: 50
Kirchhoff formula OurBigBook.com
Extend lower-dimensional data independently of an extra coordinate and apply the higher-dimensional wave equation solution. Projecting a three-dimensional sphere to the planar disk yields the kernel [2πt2−r2​]−1 for the two-dimensional solution with zero initial displacement. This method of descent for the wave equation explains why three-dimensional wave propagation can depend on a sphere while two-dimensional propagation depends on its interior.

Strong Huygens principle

Words: 37
Kirchhoff formula OurBigBook.com
The strong Huygens principle says that the three-dimensional wave solution at (t,x) depends only on initial data on the sphere ∣y−x∣=∣t∣. A compactly supported disturbance therefore leaves no tail in the interior of its light cone.

Finite propagation speed

Words: 150 Articles: 3
Wave equation OurBigBook.com
Finite propagation speed means that data outside the backward light cone of a spacetime point cannot affect the solution at that point.

Weak Huygens principle

Words: 51
Finite propagation speed OurBigBook.com
The weak Huygens principle is the domain-of-dependence statement that initial data outside a backward light cone cannot influence its tip. It permits an interior tail and is weaker than the Strong Huygens principle. For utt​−Δu+V(x)u=0 with V≥0, integrating the local energy over shrinking balls proves this statement: the boundary contribution is ut​∂ν​u−21​(ut2​+∣∇u∣2+Vu2)≤0.

Shrinking cone energy argument

Words: 42
Finite propagation speed OurBigBook.com
For the homogeneous speed-one wave equation, integrate its wave energy density over B(x∗​,T−t). The moving boundary contributes −e, while the usual flux contributes ut​∂n​u. Their sum is −21​(ut​−∂n​u)2−21​∣∇tan​u∣2≤0. Zero Cauchy data in the initial ball therefore force zero solution in its backward light cone.

Finite propagation speed OurBigBook.com
For Cauchy data prescribed on x=0 over ∣y∣<a<1, put S=artanha. The maximal region determined solely by those data is
{(x,y):∣x∣+∣artanhy∣<S}.
(3)
In the travel-time coordinate for a one-dimensional variable-speed wave equation (x,s) this is the ordinary characteristic diamond ∣x∣+∣s∣<S, as follows from finite propagation speed.

A radiation field is the rescaled limit of a wave along null infinity. For a three-dimensional wave, the outgoing field is the limit of ru(t,rω) with t−r fixed, while the incoming field fixes t+r.

A scattering map sends incoming asymptotic data to outgoing asymptotic data for the same solution.

Wave equation OurBigBook.com
The one-dimensional wave equation has left-moving and right-moving travelling-wave solutions. Their superposition is described by the D'Alembert formula and remains valid distributionally for locally integrable profiles.

The d'Alembert operator is the Lorentzian wave operator □=ημν∂μ​∂ν​ in flat spacetime, or □=∇μ∇μ​ on scalar fields in curved spacetime.

Wave equation OurBigBook.com
A semilinear wave equation has the form
utt​−Δu=F(u,∇u),
(4)

Wave map (□ϕ=ϕ(∣ϕt​∣2−∣∇ϕ∣2))

Words: 331 Articles: 6
Semilinear wave equation OurBigBook.com
A wave map is a harmonic map with Lorentzian domain: a critical point of the action obtained by contracting the pullback target metric with the domain Lorentzian metric. For target sphere S2 in Euclidean space and □=−∂t2​+Δ, its extrinsic equation is □ϕ=ϕ(∣ϕt​∣2−∣∇ϕ∣2), subject to ∣ϕ∣=1. The derivative contractions are null forms for wave equations. Wave map Cauchy data must include a tangent initial velocity.

Small data global regularity for wave maps

Words: 63
Wave map OurBigBook.com
Smooth compatible data sufficiently small in high weighted Sobolev norms relative to a constant map produce global smooth wave maps in three and four spatial dimensions. In four dimensions, derivative decay (1+t)−3/2 is time-integrable and closes commuted wave energy estimates. In three dimensions the weaker (1+t)−1 decay requires the cancellation of null forms for wave equations, exploited by the vector field method for wave equations. These classical localized-data statements do not assert global regularity from small supercritical energy alone.

Global regularity for one-dimensional wave maps

Words: 47
Wave map OurBigBook.com
For smooth localized compatible wave map Cauchy data and compact Riemannian target, one-dimensional wave maps stay smooth globally. In null coordinates, the equation is Dv​ϕu​=Du​ϕv​=0. Compatibility of the target metric with the covariant derivative makes ∣ϕu​∣2 independent of v and ∣ϕv​∣2 independent of u. These transported derivative bounds and higher energy estimates prevent finite-time breakdown.

Stationary wave map (ΔQ+∣∇Q∣2Q=0)

Words: 35
Wave map OurBigBook.com
A time-independent wave map is a harmonic map of its spatial domain into the target. For target S2, its equation is ΔQ+∣∇Q∣2Q=0. In two dimensions inverse stereographic projection gives a smooth nonconstant example of finite wave map energy 4π.

Wave map energy (E=21​∫(∣ϕt​∣2+∣∇ϕ∣2)dx)

Words: 78 Articles: 1
Wave map OurBigBook.com
The conserved energy of a wave map from Minkowski spacetime to a Riemannian target is E=21​∫(∣ϕt​∣2+∣∇ϕ∣2)dx, with norms measured in the target metric. Contraction of the wave map equation with the velocity and integration by parts gives conservation.
Wave map energy and criticality (E(ϕλ​)=λn−2E(ϕ))
Words: 47
Wave map energy OurBigBook.com
Under ϕλ​(t,x)=ϕ(t/λ,x/λ), the conserved wave map energy scales as λn−2E. Energy is subcritical for n=1, critical for n=2, and supercritical for n≥3. The critical derivative index of the homogeneous Sobolev space is sc​=n/2. Small energy alone is not an appropriate general small-data regularity hypothesis in supercritical dimensions.

Wave map Cauchy data

Words: 53
Wave map OurBigBook.com
Initial position ϕ0​ for a wave map takes values in the target, and initial velocity ϕ1​ belongs to its tangent space at ϕ0​(x). For S2 this means ∣ϕ0​∣=1 and ϕ0​⋅ϕ1​=0. Localized data agree with a constant map and zero velocity outside a compact set; the map itself need not be a compactly supported ambient function.

Null form for wave equations (Q0​(f,g)=−ft​gt​+∇f⋅∇g)

Words: 103 Articles: 1
Semilinear wave equation OurBigBook.com
A quadratic derivative expression is a null form when its symbol vanishes on parallel null covectors. The Lorentz contraction Q0​(f,g)=−ft​gt​+∇f⋅∇g is the basic example. Its cancellation suppresses interactions of derivatives pointing along the same light ray. It is the algebraic structure behind the classical null condition for wave equations.

Classical null condition for wave equations (Aαβℓα​ℓβ​=0for null ℓ)

Words: 58
Null form for wave equations OurBigBook.com
For a quadratic derivative source Aαβ∂α​u∂β​u, the classical null condition is Aαβℓα​ℓβ​=0 whenever −ℓ02​+∣ℓsp​∣2=0. It removes the leading interaction of parallel lightlike derivatives. In three dimensions this structure gives global smooth solutions for sufficiently small, localized data through the vector field method for wave equations. This PDE condition is distinct from the null condition asserting that a single vector is lightlike.

Focusing semilinear wave equation (utt​−Δu=u∣u∣p−1)

Words: 88 Articles: 1
Semilinear wave equation OurBigBook.com
The focusing power wave equation is utt​−Δu=u∣u∣p−1. Its conserved energy has the negative potential term −∣u∣p+1/(p+1) and is not positive definite. Localized ordinary differential equation blowup for a wave equation produces smooth compactly supported data with finite maximal lifespan for suitable focusing powers.

Localized ordinary differential equation blowup for a wave equation

Words: 55
Focusing semilinear wave equation OurBigBook.com
A spatially constant blowup profile for a wave equation solves an ordinary differential equation. Choose smooth compactly supported initial data which agree with the profile on a ball larger than its blowup time times the wave speed. Finite propagation speed preserves agreement in an interior light cone, forcing finite-time breakdown of the localized solution. For utt​−Δu=u3, the profile u(t)=2​/(1−t) is one example.

Smooth continuation criterion for semilinear wave equations

Words: 63
Semilinear wave equation OurBigBook.com
For a smooth semilinear wave equation whose nonlinearity is a smooth function of the solution and its first derivatives, local Sobolev space theory gives a continuation criterion: a finite maximal existence time requires divergence of a sufficiently high solution norm. A bounded base norm Hs+1×Hs, with s>n/2, allows restarting local existence. Higher regularity persists by differentiated energy estimates. Precise norms can be weakened for particular nonlinearities.

Almost global existence for wave equations (Tε​≳exp(c/ε))

Words: 55
Semilinear wave equation OurBigBook.com
Almost global existence means a lifespan which grows exponentially in the inverse size of small initial data, typically Tε​≥exp(c/ε)−1 for derivative-quadratic semilinear wave equations in three dimensions. Commuted wave energy and the Klainerman-Sobolev inequality lead to a logarithmic accumulation εlog(1+T) in a bootstrap argument. This implies existence up to every fixed inverse power ε−N when the data are small enough depending on N.

E(u)=∫(2∣ut​∣2+∣∇u∣2​+p+1∣u∣p+1​)dx.

Words: 42
Defocusing semilinear wave equation OurBigBook.com
For utt​−Δu+u3=0 in three spatial dimensions, conserved positive wave energy E controls ∥∇u∥2​. The Sobolev inequality gives ∥u2∇u∥2​≲∥∇u∥22​∥D2u∥2​≲E∥D2u∥2​. Differentiated wave energy estimates and the Gronwall inequality then give ∥u(t)∥H˙2​+∥ut​(t)∥H˙1​≤CDeCEt, where D bounds the corresponding initial Sobolev norms.

For phase kx+mz−ωt with k=0, hold z fixed: a contour of constant wave phase advances in x at ω/k. This is the speed at which a tilted wavefront crosses a horizontal line. It differs from the horizontal component of the vector phase velocity, ωk/(k2+m2), which is defined along the wavevector.
Phase speed (∣ω∣/∣k∣)
Words: 29
Phase velocity OurBigBook.com
The magnitude of the phase velocity of a real-frequency plane Fourier mode is ∣ω∣/∣k∣. In an anisotropic medium it depends on the direction of the wave vector and need not equal the group velocity magnitude.

Group velocity

Words: 27
Phase velocity and group velocity OurBigBook.com
Group velocity is the gradient of angular frequency with respect to wavevector, cg​=∇k​ω. It gives the leading propagation velocity of a narrow wave packet.

Crest and trough

Words: 45 Articles: 2
Phase velocity and group velocity OurBigBook.com
The wave crest and wave trough are respectively the highest and lowest displacements in a wave.
Wave crest
Words: 24
Crest and trough OurBigBook.com
A wave crest is a local maximum of the wave's displacement. In a monochromatic travelling wave it lies at a fixed phase and propagates at the phase velocity.
Wave trough
Words: 9
Crest and trough OurBigBook.com
A wave trough is a local minimum of the wave's displacement.

Wave packet

Words: 45 Articles: 1
Phase velocity and group velocity OurBigBook.com
A wave packet is a localized superposition of nearby wavenumbers. Its envelope propagates at the group velocity to leading order.
Envelope (waves)
Words: 25
Wave packet OurBigBook.com
A wave envelope is a slowly varying amplitude multiplying a rapidly oscillating carrier wave. Its variation describes localization, modulation, growth, or attenuation of the carrier.

Exponential initial-velocity tail for the Klein-Gordon equation (u(x,t)=te−∣x∣(∣x∣>t))

Words: 63
Klein-Gordon equation OurBigBook.com
For utt​=uxx​−u with u(x,0)=0 and ut​(x,0)=e−∣x∣, the solution outside ∣x∣≤t is exactly te−∣x∣. On the positive half-line, te−x satisfies both the equation and initial data; the finite propagation speed limits dependence at x>t to positive initial points. Uniqueness on this domain of dependence proves the formula there, and reflection gives the negative half-line. The exterior tail is nonzero because the initial velocity is not compactly supported.

Stationary-phase asymptotic of a Klein-Gordon wave along a subluminal ray

Words: 62 Articles: 1
Klein-Gordon equation OurBigBook.com
For zero initial velocity and Fourier amplitude a(k), observation along x=Vt with 0≤V<c selects the two stationary wavenumbers ±k0​, where
k0​=c2−V2​AV​.
(29)
Writing s=c2−V2​, the leading oscillation has angular frequency As and amplitude proportional to t−1/2.
